text:
Maya: heads up — eu-west1 gpu pending spike starting ~03:02 UTC, dozens of tiny training pods pending
Sam: saw the grafana alert, cluster autoscaler kicked but pods stayed Pending
Devon: dug into events: scale-up created nodes but kubelet failed join on 3 new hosts, CNI errors + networkpolicy denies between kube-controller and new nodes
Maya: logs from one node:
```
Mar 03 03:08 kubelet[1]: failed to register node: error dialing kube-apiserver: network unreachable
Mar 03 03:09 containerd: failed to setup pod network: Calico policy deny
```
Sam: so autoscaler did its job but networkpolicy prevented kube-proxy/CNI from initializing, nodes remained NotReady
Infra-bot: Alert: 8 nodes requested, 5 registered, 3 NotReady > 10m
Aurora: the weird part — these racks have recently had a firewall profile change (infra-rollout yesterday), maybe a misapplied rule for the eu-west1-b subnet
Lina: can confirm firewall change: egress ACL now blocks 10.0.0.0/16 -> control-plane on one of the rack subnets, likely the culprit
Devon: timeline: 03:02 scale request -> 03:06 cloud provider provision -> 03:06-03:14 nodes try to join -> 03:14 join finally after ACL rollback manual fix -> 03:20 many pods evicted/recreated and starvation for gpu small-slot queues
Maya: eviction ripple: because new nodes didn't join, scheduler backfilled other racks and triggered affinity/taint evictions — saw many tiny gpu pods preempted for larger reserved jobs
Sam: cost hit: extra burst capacity + re-scheduling churn = ~500 GPU-minutes wasted during the incident window (estimate)
Aurora: short term mitigation: 1) add pre-join network checks in node bootstrap, 2) autoscaler should mark nodes as failed if join > 6m, 3) make a temporary exemption for control-plane access for provisioning subnets
Lina: longer term: add admission webhook that rejects networkpolicy updates that would block cluster-join paths (or at least flag in PR)
Devon: scheduler side: we should tweak the late-bind logic to avoid aggressive global backfill when expected node join latency > threshold — maybe queue tiny gpu pods in warm-pool preferred until join confirmed
Maya: can we also reduce eviction aggressiveness for tiny pods in gpu-pool? They are cheap to keep and reduce churn costs
Sam: +1. proposal: relax preemption threshold for pods with label `gpu.workload=small` and prefer soft-affinity to reduce resechdule waves
Infra-bot: Note: rolling back firewall ACL was the immediate fix at 03:14. Postmortem scheduled in #postmortems, please drop timeline + logs
Aurora: i'll open a follow-up RFC for the webhook + autoscaler tweak, tagging scheduler and security teams
Lina: uploading node bootstrap logs to the incident folder now -> link: https://internal.redwood/incident/1732104444/logs
Maya: thanks — i'll add a quick runbook step to check ACLs before approving infra rollouts to racks with GPUs :thumbsup:
Devon: thanks team. action items: rollback guard, autoscaler timeout, scheduler late-bind tweak, eviction policy for small gpu pods. I'll track in the eng-platform backlog.
